decisions.decision: Two steps: Cliente → Cotización, not a single screen with a customer gate
decisions.why: A quote cannot be opened without an explicit customer (the server defaults it to Público en General), and a customer-as-gate on one screen is the pattern 039 is replacing
decisions.rejected: One step with the customer as a CustomerBar gate, matching todays OrderScreen

decisions.decision: Converting a quote lands the user in the back-office order workspace on the Venta (goods) step
decisions.why: The converted order arrives with no fulfilment intent and no warehouse on any line, so it is not finishable as it stands
decisions.rejected: Landing on a read-only order detail, or staying on the quote with a link

decisions.decision: Quote line prices stay read-only; absolute price_adjustment is deferred, not dropped
decisions.why: Conversion folds price_adjustment into price anyway, so anything expressible as a markup is expressible as a discount; adopting it would diverge the quote host from the other two capture hosts for no v1 gain
decisions.rejected: An editable price / showPriceAdjustment flag on the shared line row

decisions.decision: The quotes list shows all quotes in the facility by default, not only the current users
decisions.why: Matches how the orders list behaves today and suits a back office where quoting is a shared activity
decisions.rejected: Defaulting to the API mine filter, as legacy did

concerns.note: Hard dependency on 039-back-office-order-workspace: the shared capture step is host-agnostic only after 039, and conversion lands in the workspace 039 creates. Both features edit the same capture files, so parallel branches will conflict.
mbe-api#213 degrades the list story: quote rows carry no customer name and list search silently ignores non-numeric terms. Does not block P1.
mbe-api#209 does not account for orders raised by quote conversion; raised upstream. Affects only whether a converted order is distinguishable from a register sale on a list row.

expectations: Payment and delivery on the quote itself
Printing, PDF and email of a quote — no server-side rendering exists, and the sibling printing effort does not currently scope quotes
Absolute per-line price adjustment (deferred, not dropped)
Profit-margin and credit checks on quotes
Changing the orders list to show that an order came from a quote
